explanation: Lebanese families brought spit-roasted lamb, cooked like shawarma, to cities such as Puebla. Mexican cooks swapped in chilli-marinated pork and often crown the spit with a pineapple.

claims.text: Tacos al pastor developed in Mexico from the spit-roasted shawarma brought by Lebanese immigrants.
Tacos al pastor did not grow out of the cooking of Greek, Italian or Chinese immigrants to Mexico.
Lebanese immigrants brought spit-roasted meat cooked in the shawarma style to Mexican cities such as Puebla, where it became known as tacos árabes.
Tacos al pastor use pork marinated with chillies instead of lamb, and the spit is often topped with a pineapple.
